Want to sell machines that give plastic a second life?

Join one of Europe’s leading suppliers of used plastic machinery as our new Sales Representative.

We’re looking for an experienced salesperson who enjoys working with technical machinery and international customers. Euro Machinery buys and sells new and used converting and plastic recycling machines on a global scale.

Supported by a passionate and experienced international team, we work closely together to identify the best machines on the market for our customers.

Job description:

You will play an important part in our sales strategy and be responsible for driving sales of new and used machinery and equipment in dedicated markets.

If you are a dynamic and proactive professional with a passion for sales and a commitment to teamwork, we would like to hear from you.

Our new Sales Representative will be working from our main office in Vissenbjerg, Denmark.

However, we work on a global platform and you can expect to travel approximately 30 days per year to visit customers and attend trade shows.

Key Responsibilities:

• Develop and execute your own strategic sales plan in collaboration with our team.

• Identify and pursue new customers in your markets.

• Collaborate with cross-functional team members on projects.

• Provide market insights and feedback to contribute to business development and marketing initiatives.

• Represent the company at industry events and trade shows.

Qualifications:

• A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

• Proven track record of successful sales performance.

• Good understanding of machinery or equivalent technical solutions.

• Excellent communication and negotiation skills.

• Experience working with CRM systems.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a global team.

• Professional-level English; Danish is a plus.

We are looking for someone who:

• Enjoy building relationships and understands customer needs.

• Bring positive energy and look for solutions rather than obstacles.

• Are open-minded and tolerant towards other cultures and backgrounds.

• Have residence within reasonable commuting distance of our office in Vissenbjerg.

We can offer:

• Competitive salary and performance-based bonuses.

• Opportunities for professional development and growth.

• A collaborative and inclusive work environment.

• An exciting job with an international outlook.

You are welcome to read more about our company here: https://www.euromachinery.com/about-us/ If you have any questions about the position, please call CEO Belinda Frederiksen on +45 30870225 or email to belinda.f@euro-machinery.com. Please send your application, cover letter and CV to Belinda, or apply directly through this LinkedIn advertisement.

NG Nordic is a leading provider of circular solutions and environmental services in the Nordics. By transforming waste into valuable resources and removing hazardous substances from the material cycle, we reduce emissions, protect natural ecosystems, and increase access to circular materials. NG Nordic is an important part of the Nordic industrial infrastructure, generating revenue of EUR 1.3 billion with a team of around 3,400 employees and 90 facilities.

Health & Safety Specialist, Nyborg, Denmark

Do you want to be the Safety Shoulder and make a real difference to safety in one of Europe’s most complex industrial environments?

Be the trusted Health & Safety voice in daily operations at NG Nordic’s hazardous waste treatment facility in Nyborg.

As Health & Safety Specialist, you will work close to the operational teams, helping managers and employees turn safety requirements into practical actions. You will be part of a five-person team in Nyborg and work as an integrated partner to Operations.

Nyborg is a Seveso III facility and is described as the EU’s largest hazardous waste treatment plant. Here, health and safety is not simply a compliance exercise: the risks are real, and your work can have a direct impact on people, processes and operational reliability.

Your role combines visible presence in the plant with reporting, statistics, procedures, training and improvement projects. You will advise and challenge Operations constructively, build trust across functions and help ensure a safe, professional operation.

The position is based in Nyborg and requires regular engagement with employees, supervisors and managers throughout the facility.

You will turn safety requirements into practical improvements in daily operations

You will participate in daily and weekly operational meetings, identify and prioritise EHSQ risks, and help the organisation address the issues that matter most. You will balance proactive safety work with administrative responsibilities and timely follow-up.

Your key tasks will include:

• Acting as the Health & Safety partner to Operations, advising managers and employees and participating in daily and weekly operational meetings

• Conducting safety walks, workplace inspections, toolbox talks and awareness activities, and following up on identified risks

• Preparing safety reports, statistics and KPI follow-up, identifying trends and recommending actions

• Developing and implementing practical safety procedures, training programmes, onboarding and contractor inductions

• Supporting risk assessments, audits, investigations and structured root-cause analyses of incidents and near misses

• Driving and prioritising safety improvement projects, monitoring corrective actions and supporting compliance with Danish legislation, internal standards and Seveso-related requirements

Experience from health and safety in industrial operations

We imagine that you have a relevant technical or health and safety qualification and approximately five years or more of experience in a comparable operational environment. Experience from process industry, chemicals, hazardous waste, energy or other high-risk facilities is especially relevant.

You understand occupational health and safety legislation, operational risk assessments, incident investigation, safety management systems and the importance of effective training and documentation. You are comfortable working with reports, statistics and digital tools.

You can translate complex safety requirements into clear, workable solutions. You communicate confidently in Danish and English, both verbally and in writing, and you know how to engage colleagues across functions and organisational levels.

You build credibility through presence, sound judgement and constructive dialogue. You have the natural authority to challenge unsafe practices while maintaining trust and respect, and you are robust enough to handle disagreement and pressure.

You are structured, proactive and able to prioritise competing tasks. You enjoy combining hands-on operational work with analysis, administration and continuous improvement, always keeping the most significant risks in focus.

Interested?

If you want to help create a safer and more professional operation in an environment where safety genuinely matters, we would like to hear from you.

NG Nordic is partnering with Brinch & Partners on this recruitment. For questions about the role, contact Partner Jens Chr. Jensen at +45 7020 2328. Please submit your CV and application in English.

We interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

All enquiries will be treated confidentially.

We want our recruitment process to be fair and inclusive. That is why we do not ask for photos or lengthy cover letters. Instead, we use screening questions to ensure comparable applications. We do, however, ask for gender information to help us ensure good gender balance in the recruitment process.

Would you like to shape the people, culture and organisational foundations of one of the world’s leading humanitarian organisations?

This is an opportunity to bring your global leadership experience to a mission with profound human impact. As Executive Director for People & Organisation (P&O) at the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), you will inspire employees, empower leaders and turn strategy into meaningful change – ensuring that DRC has the people, capabilities, structures and safeguards required to deliver effective humanitarian responses wherever they are needed most.

You will join DRC at an important time and have a real opportunity to influence its global direction and organisation. The global humanitarian system is going through fundamental change, and you will help shape and adapt organisational structure, operating models and staff capacity to the challenges and opportunities of the future. Your portfolio is global and spans organisation and culture, HR and leadership development, surge capacity, safety, legal affairs and Code of Conduct. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help shape strategy, and you will lead approximately 200 colleagues across P&O functions in headquarters and countries.

**About The Job

**Reporting directly to the Secretary General, you will set the direction for DRC’s global People & Organisation strategy and ensure that it becomes an enabler for DRC’s ambitions. In close partnership with the Executive Management Team and senior leaders, you will create the conditions for talented people to grow and thrive – while strengthening an inclusive, and high-performing culture.

This role calls for a leader who enjoys moving between strategic ambition and practical delivery. You will ensure that global policies, systems, data, employment conditions and governance provide relevant and timely support to operations. At the same time, you will carry executive accountability for safeguarding, ethical conduct, legal compliance, safety and DRC’s humanitarian surge capacity – areas fundamental to DRC’s mission.

You will lead and develop an experienced senior team; Global HR, HR Denmark, HR Operations & Analytics, Surge Capacity, Safety, Code of Conduct, Legal, management support, and change, leadership and culture. Based at DRC’s headquarters in Copenhagen, you will work across a global organisation and build trusted relationships with colleagues and partners from many cultures and contexts.

The impact you will make:

• Shape DRC’s strategy, culture and global P&O agenda.

• Lead organisational change, leadership development and employee engagement.

• Attract, develop and retain the people DRC needs to deliver its mission.

• Ensure effective global P&O policies, systems, services and people insights.

• Oversee safeguarding, Code of Conduct, safety, legal compliance, duty of care.

• Strengthen humanitarian surge capacity.

**About You

**You are a credible executive who is motivated by purpose and energised by complexity. You bring the strategic perspective to see the whole organisation, the judgement to make thoughtful choices and the drive to translate ambition into clear priorities and measurable results. Colleagues experience you as an inclusive and trusted leader with integrity and empathy providing the clarity to make decisions and create momentum.

What you will bring:

• 10+ years of senior experience in global organisations and people leadership.

• A strong record of shaping people strategy and leading transformation across complex, international operations.

• Experience of organisational development, including the renewal and design of operating models.

• Broad understanding of governance, compliance, safeguarding, safety and legal matters.

• Strong stakeholder management, analytical and communication skills.

• An inclusive, decisive and high-integrity leadership style.

• A relevant master’s degree and fluent English; additional competency in French, Spanish, Arabic and Danish are an advantage.

All employees in DRC should master DRC's core competencies: Communicating, Taking the lead, Collaborating, Striving for excellence and Demonstrating integrity.

**We offer

**Contract length: Permanent

Work location:  Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken S-train station. DRC has recently moved to a newly renovated multi-tenant house (VOX) with a modern look and shared green canteen.

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and Lederaftalen between Dansk Arbejdsgiverforening and Lederne (agreement for managers), which can be found here: www.lederne.dk. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

**Application process

**If you are motivated by the opportunity to strengthen a global humanitarian organisation through its people, culture and organisational capabilities, we would welcome your application. Korn Ferry is assisting the Danish Refugee Council with the recruitment of the Executive Director, People & Organisation. Please submit your motivated application and CV through the designated recruitment channel. All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

Closing date for applications: Wednesday 11th November 2026

Further information For questions regarding the vacancy please contact: Rabea Rehman, Associate | Executive Search at Korn Ferry, E: DRC_PO@KornFerry.com

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website drc.ngo .

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

Are you a recent or upcoming graduate interested in making an impact? Become part of a global and successful MedTech company located in the heart of Copenhagen.

About 3Shape

Things have moved fast at 3Shape ever since our founding in 2000. 3Shape specializes in developing 3D scanning and software technology solutions that enable dental and hearing professionals to treat more people more effectively, and with improved care. Every second of every day, a 3Shape scanner is used all around the globe. A number which is skyrocketing and cementing our position as technology and industry leader, Danish growth comet and unicorn company. We are a truly international workplace with 50+ nationalities and more than 2200 employees globally. We are headquartered in Denmark in the center of vibrant Copenhagen at Kongens Nytorv.

About the 3Shape 2-Year Graduate Program

3Shape’s two-year Graduate Program serves as a launchpad for a high-impact career. Graduates rotate through three different departments within the Commercial Track, with the possibility of an international assignment. This program gives talented and motivated young professionals the chance to acquire new knowledge, expand their skillset, and gain valuable expertise from the very beginning. Graduates gain unique insights into the core of our business and play an essential role in our strategy to develop future leaders and specialists at 3Shape.

Become Our Next Commercial Graduate

We offer a steep learning curve and expect high performance, but in return, you will have opportunities to grow both professionally and personally.

We Fuel Your Career With

• Quarterly graduate-community activities.

What Makes a 3Shape Graduate?

You are about to complete or have just completed a master’s degree. You have achieved top academic results and are highly proficient in English. You are enthusiastic, focused, and eager to learn.

• An excellent collaborator with an empathetic approach and a global mindset.

• Highly versatile and adaptable.

• Thrives in an international environment.

• Motivated to take responsibility.

• Strong analytical thinker with solid problem-solving skills.

• Brings positive energy and is eager to apply knowledge and make an impact.

What 3Shape Offers

• A vibrant, international environment with social, diverse, and highly skilled colleagues - over 20 nationalities represented in our Denmark-based office.

• An attractive healthcare package

• Daily breakfast and healthy lunches prepared by our private chefs.

• A good social work environment with many optional activities and clubs, from wine and beer tastings to board games, running, and paddle.

• Modern offices and R&D labs in downtown Copenhagen, near Kongens Nytorv, Nyhavn, and the Copenhagen Canals.

Application Process

• After a successful application and initial video call screening, candidates will be invited to our headquarters in Copenhagen for an assessment center on Friday, January 29th.

• If you have questions about the position or process, contact people@3shape.com.

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

**About Flatpay

**Flatpay makes card payments simple and fair for small businesses. Marketing is central to how we grow, and we run it as a measurable acquisition engine where curiosity, experimentation and commercial results drive our decisions.

We are looking for an Affiliate & Partnerships Manager to lead our network of affiliates, publishers and lead generation partners across all of our markets.

The role

In six months, affiliate went from zero to one of our most important channels. Now we need someone to take it further.

You like meeting people, spotting opportunities and turning a good conversation into a partnership that performs. You can negotiate a strong deal and still leave the other side wanting to work with you again. And signing is only the start: you will follow each partnership through the funnel, understand what makes it profitable and make it better.

This is a group function. You will report to our Head of Group Marketing, work with colleagues across creative, paid media and analytics, and have real autonomy. We want fewer approval steps, not more. You will need to be self-driven, and in return you will learn a lot across teams and functions.

**What You'll Do

**

• Find new partners. Identify promising affiliates, publishers and lead generation partners, start the conversations and build a pipeline across our markets.

• Negotiate deals that last. Agree pricing, commission structures and terms that support profitable growth for us and a sustainable relationship for them.

• Turn good partners into great ones. Set clear expectations and help partners improve their campaigns, placements and results.

• Look beyond the lead. Follow the journey from lead to booked meeting to customer, and weigh acquisition cost against customer value.

• Make the call. Recommend when to scale, renegotiate, pause or end a partnership.

• Fix what is leaking. Work with partners, the analytics team and sales to find where performance breaks down, then test hypotheses.

• Own the roadmap and reporting. Set the partner roadmap, run onboarding, tracking and commission validation, and report on what the channel delivers.

• Work smarter with AI. Use AI as an assistant to find partners, analyse results and speed up daily work. It supports your judgement and never replaces it.

**How We Work

**

• Quality first, then scale. We would rather have fewer, better leads than many weak ones, but we are not afraid to test. One high-potential partner was trialled in one market and, two months later, was live in five and our biggest partner in the group.

• Shared decisions where it counts. You will set commission models and budgets together with the Head of Group Marketing, so we stay aligned across channels.

**Who You Are

**

• You have experience in affiliate marketing, performance partnerships or lead generation, with responsibility for partner relationships and measurable results.

• You are a strong negotiator who understands the other side’s incentives and can have a direct conversation when something needs to change.

• You are commercially sharp and comfortable turning data and spreadsheets into a clear recommendation.

• You are curious. You ask why, test your assumptions and change your mind when the evidence says so.

• You take initiative and follow through, and you are happy moving fast where not every process exists yet.

• You communicate clearly in English. Additional languages are a plus.

Experience with B2B lead generation, platforms such as Impact, Awin or PartnerStack, or tracking and attribution is an advantage. We can more about your judgement, results and ability to learn than about tool familiarity.

What we offer

• Real ownership of the partner roadmap and a direct hand in growing a channel that grows with the company

• Competitive salary based on your qualifications

• A central marketing team and a manager who will support your development

• Room to build processes, try new approaches and shape the future of affiliate at Flatpay

**Why Flatpay

**Joining Flatpay means stepping into a dynamic environment where innovation is encouraged, and teamwork is celebrated. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, contributing to our mission of empowering merchants to succeed.

With us, you’ll experience an ambitious drive to constantly push boundaries and redefine what's possible. While we don’t take ourselves too seriously, we take our responsibility towards our people very seriously. We welcome driven, low-ego individuals who live our values and want to grow with us.

Established in 2022 in Copenhagen with a commitment to transparency, we've streamlined card payments to small and medium-sized businesses. Our innovative pricing model eliminates hidden costs and fees, offering a simple flat rate for all cards with no monthly subscription for our point-of-sale and payment solutions.

Operating in Denmark, Finland, Germany, Italy, France, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, we're more than just a service provider; we are your trusted business partner.

We continuously strive to stay ahead of the curve, adapting our solutions to meet our clients' evolving needs. Ready to be part of something extraordinary?

We amplify what organizations of any size can see, do, and achieve with video. Guided by our People First mindset - freedom, inclusion, and togetherness - we always consider our employees, partners, and communities in everything we do.

Make an impact with us

At Milestone Systems, what you do matters. People are at the heart of everything we do, grounded in integrity, collaboration, strong relationships, and a curiosity that drives continuous learning. It is how we work together, learn from one another, embrace new perspectives, and create lasting impact.

In this role, you will be a trusted partner to managers and teams, helping them turn business priorities into value adding people actions. You will create impact through thoughtful coaching, strong relationships and the confidence to help managers build strong teams.

About the role

As People Partner, you will own the people partnership for your assigned business areas. You will work closely with managers, leadership teams and, when relevant, their teams to strengthen leadership, engagement, performance and organisational effectiveness.

You will report to the Head of People & Culture HQ and become part of our global People & Culture team, collaborating with colleagues across regions and specialist areas.

What makes this role interesting is the breadth. One day you may coach a manager through a sensitive performance conversation; the next, you may facilitate a leadership-team workshop, support a recruitment process or turn engagement insights into focused action. You will have room to influence, while staying close to the managers and teams you support.

What you will do

• Partner with managers, leadership teams and, when relevant, their teams to understand business priorities and translate them into focused people plans and actions.

• Coach and challenge managers on leadership dilemmas, team effectiveness, engagement, development and retention, building their confidence to lead well.

• Guide managers through employee relations and performance matters including difficult conversations, performance improvement plans, disciplinary issues and terminations, with clear documentation and sound judgement.

• Drive key people processes such as talent reviews, performance management, annual salary review and individual development follow-up.

• Use people data and insight including engagement results and workforce information, to identify priorities, support decisions and follow through on actions.

• Support organisation design, workforce planning and change by facilitating discussions, challenging assumptions and helping leaders make sustainable decisions.

• Support recruitment and facilitate team interventions by partnering with hiring managers on recruitments, and by planning and facilitating workshops for leadership teams and employee groups.

What you bring

We are looking for someone with:

• 5-8 years of experience as an HR Business Partner, People Partner or in a comparable broad people role, ideally in an international or matrix organisation.

• Strong experience coaching and advising managers at different levels, with the credibility to be supportive, candid and appropriately challenging.

• Hands-on experience with performance management and employee relations, including sensitive conversations, performance improvement and organisational change.

• A good understanding of talent, engagement, workforce planning, organisation design and reward processes, and how these areas connect to business outcomes.

• The ability to use people data to spot patterns, frame choices and support practical decision-making.

• Strong facilitation, communication and stakeholder-management skills, with fluency in English.

• A relevant degree or equivalent practical experience in HR, People & Culture, business or organisational development.

How you will make a difference

• You will thrive in this role if you are curious about the business, easy to work with and motivated by helping managers succeed rather than taking ownership away from them.

• You build trust quickly, keep momentum when topics are complex and can move comfortably between strategic perspective and hands-on support.

• You are decisive and comfortable working independently, while knowing that support and sparring from colleagues are always close at hand.

• You bring empathy to sensitive situations, but you are also clear, pragmatic and willing to challenge when it matters.

Meet the team

You’ll join People & Culture HQ, a collaborative team of 6, working closely with managers, employees and specialist colleagues across Milestone. We care about making People & Culture support useful, consistent and close to the business.

We share perspectives, help each other and keep things practical. You will have space to shape your partnerships and contribute to how our People Partner model continues to develop.

How we support you

At Milestone, we want you to have the opportunity to do meaningful work, develop your skills and grow your career.

We offer you:

• Individual development plans aligned with your career goals

• Access to training, learning resources, and certifications

• Flexible working arrangements

• Supportive leadership and regular feedback

• Opportunities for cross-functional and cross-regional collaboration

• Social activities and spaces to connect with colleagues

Ready to make an impact?

If you are excited about working closely with managers and teams, shaping meaningful people solutions and helping leaders navigate both opportunities and difficult moments, we would love to hear from you.

Questions about the role? Feel free to contact Head of People & Culture HQ, Britt Jørgensen, at brj@milestone.dk

We are seeking a professionally strong and dedicated  Chef /  Chef to join our kitchen team. You will act as a key partner to the restaurant and share responsibility for the daily operations, quality assurance, and continued development of the kitchen.

jobs.description:
A clinical position as staff specialist of Paediatrics at the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position as staff specialist is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical associate professor (research) in Paediatrics at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

With this new position the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Zealand University Hospital wishes to strengthen the leadership in clinical research and teaching in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the clinical associate professorship (research) and the clinical position.

About the Department

The Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is a well-established clinical and research-active department with sites in Roskilde (planned move to Køge 2028) and Nykøbing Falster. The department provides comprehensive care across the full spectrum of paediatrics, including specialised services within paediatric endocrinology and the management of childhood diabetes.

The treatment of childhood diabetes in Region Zealand is organised across multiple sites, enabling strong cross-site collaboration and the development of shared clinical pathways. The department works closely with Steno Diabetes Center Zealand and collaborates with paediatric departments both within and beyond the region.

The department offers a dynamic research environment with a focus on strengthening clinical research, including dedicated research within childhood diabetes. This field involves distinct clinical and developmental considerations compared to adult diabetes, and research activities address treatment outcomes, patient development, quality of life and health equality.

Teaching and supervision of medical students and junior doctors are integral parts of the department’s activities, and there is a strong emphasis on developing future clinicians and clinical researchers.

Qualifications:

Applicants for a position as staff specialist must be board-certified specialist in Paediatrics.

Conditions:

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the clinical associate professorship (research)) and to the hospital (the clinical position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the clinical associate professorship (research). Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as staff specialists at Zealand University Hospital.

Salary and conditions of employment as staff specialist are as agreed between the Danish Regions and the Danish Association of Medical Specialists and between the Capital Region/Region Zealand and University of Copenhagen.

As clinical associate professor (research) at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g. research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine.

Application procedure:

The application must include the following:

• Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• A description of how the applicant is qualified as

- Clinical expert

- Communicator

- Collaborator

- Manager/administrator/organizer

- Health advocate

- Scholar/researcher/teacher, professional

For more information please refer to https://sundhedsstyrelsen.dk/en/news/2013/the-seven-roles-of-physicians.

For applicants with a foreign license also a copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Paediatrics recognition.

The closing date for applications is 30.11.2026.

jobs.description:
**Shape the engineering solutions behind vaccines that protect lives every day

**Are you an experienced bioprocess engineer who combines deep technical expertise with the ability to set direction and bring people together?

Join Bavarian Nordic and take a leading role in shaping the processes and systems that support our Drug Substance manufacturing.

From major capital projects and technology transfers to solving complex manufacturing challenges, you will help ensure our processes are robust, scalable, and ready for reliable operation.

**Your impact

**As Senior Engineering Specialist, you will serve as a technical authority for integrated bioprocess systems across process engineering, automation, filtration, and equipment design.

You will guide critical technical decisions throughout the manufacturing lifecycle—from concept and scale-up through qualification, validation, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad technical responsibility and influence across functions and projects. You will lead technical workstreams and mentor experienced engineers without formal line-management responsibility.

**What You Will Do

**Working closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Automation, Quality, Validation, and external partners, you will:

• Lead bioprocess design and optimization: Set the technical direction for upstream and downstream processes, purification, bulk formulation, and sterile transfers. Use process knowledge, modelling, and manufacturing data to improve yield, capacity, reliability, and product quality.

• Shape automation and control strategies: Translate process needs into requirements for PLC/DCS and SCADA systems, recipes, sequences, interlocks, and alarms. Ensure solutions support effective process control, data integrity, and reliable operation.

• Provide technical leadership for filtration: Define filter selection, sizing, validation, and integrity-testing strategies for liquid and gas systems. Lead investigations into filter failures, pressure deviations, and performance issues.

• Guide equipment and system design: Review and approve tanks, piping, pumps, valves, and instrumentation, including hydraulic calculations, pressure distribution, and pressure-testing strategies. Lead technical decisions for Cleaning-in-Place and Sterilization-in-Place (CIP/SIP) systems.

• Deliver projects and technology transfers: Lead process engineering activities from concept and vendor selection through factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, qualification, process validation, and handover to operations.

• Strengthen technical standards and compliance: Resolve complex investigations, support change controls and CAPAs, and represent engineering during audits and inspections. Establish reusable design standards and share knowledge across projects and teams.

**What You Bring

**You have a master’s degree or PhD in Bioengineering, Biochemical or Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

You bring substantial industrial experience, typically 15 years or more, including at least 10 years within pharmaceutical, biotechnology or vaccine manufacturing.

Your experience includes:

• Leading complex engineering projects as a lead engineer or technical authority, with hands-on expertise in bioprocess development, scale-up, commercial manufacturing, and lifecycle management.

• Integrating process equipment with automation and SCADA systems, including control strategies, computerized-system validation, and data integrity.

• Designing and validating filtration systems, including filter integrity testing and pressure/flow troubleshooting.

• Working with hygienic tanks and piping, hydraulic calculations, pressure testing, CIP/SIP, and contamination control.

• Leading commissioning, qualification, process validation, Process Performance Qualification, and technology transfer, supported by a strong understanding of GMP and quality risk management.

• Setting technical standards, mentoring experienced engineers, and influencing decisions across functions without relying on formal authority.

**How You Work

**You combine scientific depth with practical engineering judgement. You can move from detailed technical analysis to clear recommendations that help colleagues and leaders make informed decisions.

You take ownership, challenge assumptions constructively, and remain focused when problems span multiple systems or disciplines. Whether working with operators, specialists, suppliers, or senior stakeholders, you communicate clearly and build trust through sound decisions and consistent follow-through.

You also enjoy developing others. Sharing expertise, coaching colleagues, and creating common standards are natural parts of how you work.

**Why join Bavarian Nordic?

**At Bavarian Nordic, we work to protect lives through vaccines. In this role, you will help build and improve the manufacturing capabilities that make that purpose possible.

You will have the opportunity to influence major technical decisions, strengthen engineering practices, and see your work translate into measurable improvements in manufacturing performance and reliable supply.

Our values—Persisting Pioneers, Embracing Change, and Boosted by the Team—shape how we collaborate and solve challenges. For the right candidate, sustained performance may open opportunities for broader engineering leadership or formal people management.

**We look forward to receiving your application and learning how your technical expertise and leadership could strengthen Bavarian Nordic.

jobs.occupation: Kickstart your Career with Deloitte’s Finance Consultancy Programme
jobs.description:
Are you interested in working in an exciting and challenging consulting role, where you can deploy and develop your skills and competencies within the CFO domain of companies? Do you hold a business-related Master’s degree by the summer of 2027, and are you ready to embark on a life-long learning journey in a leading global consulting firm? If yes, then we might have the perfect opportunity for you!

Who we are

Joining our Finance Consultancy Programme, you will get to collaborate with experienced consultants on a wide variety of assignments and development opportunities. At Deloitte, we work with different project sizes across finance disciplines and industries, but the foundation is always the same: Our genuine passion for the CFO area and creating value together with our clients.

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte Technology & Transformation (former Consulting) consisting of more than 350 consultants in Denmark who work across all areas of the CFO function. We engage with clients to operate, advise, optimize, and transform their finance functions. Our clients range from domestic to international, from private to public, across various industries, sizes, and time horizons.

You will join a team that emphasizes collaboration, collegiality, coaching, and talent development. At Deloitte, we value diverse skills, experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, encouraging an inclusive and collaborative environment.

Exciting tasks await you

As an Analyst in Deloitte Finance Transformation, you will experience that no workdays are the same. You will face a wide range of tasks, both in the form of interim-based roles and project-based assignments. Projects and tasks will vary across finance disciplines (e.g., operational finance or business finance) and industries (e.g., private or public), and within the first years of your career, you will be assigned to as many different projects and tasks as possible to expand your toolbox and build on your financial craftmanship.

Based on the specific client's needs and your interests, experiences, and competencies, typical assignments and projects could be within the scope of:

• Finance operations optimization and transformation, e.g., controlling, month-end closing, and reporting

• Transformation and digitalization of finance functions, e.g., process optimization, closing excellence, internal controls advisory, and leveraging technology solutions

• Enterprise performance management, e.g., analytics, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting

• ERP-enabled finance transformations and finance systems implementation, e.g., outlining the ERP-strategy, defining business requirements and ensuring consistent data migration

• Finance strategy and operating model, e.g., designing service delivery models, outlining roles and responsibilities and conducting assessments

• M&A readiness and finance post-merger integration

• Global business services transformations, e.g., assessing, developing and implementing shared service functions and aligning service delivery with corporate strategy

• Internal business development and leadership support, e.g., assisting on client proposals, facilitating events and developing material to strengthen our market offerings.

Onboarding and learning

When joining us, you will participate in our onboarding programme designed with the purpose of giving you the best foundation for kickstarting your career in Deloitte. During your first two weeks, you and your peers will attend our Finance Transformation Nordic Bootcamp and our Consultant Academy, where the content is tailored to match your competencies as recent graduates. The Finance Transformation Bootcamp helps you in building your finance craftmanship and toolbox, while the Consultant Academy prepares you for your consulting role in Deloitte Technology & Transformation. Also heavily focused on social activities and team-building, the onboarding programme provides a smooth transition from university as it offers a unique opportunity to connect and build strong relations with your fellow new joiners from day one.

At Deloitte, we believe in life-long learning, and we are committed to investing in your individual development, both professionally and personally, throughout your career. You will experience this with our Finance Consultancy Programme, which is a highly structured learning programme, aimed at equipping you with the appropriate skillset and the right level of competencies needed to succeed in your role.

Leadership and culture

To support your learning, you will also be assigned a People Leader as your closest leader and go-to sparring partner. Your People Leader will help you set the overall direction of your journey in Deloitte and provide guidance across projects to make sure that your individual aspirations and professional development goals are met. Every career path is unique, and together with your People Leader you get the chance to shape your own.

We believe in leadership at all levels, and we have committed ourselves to creating and maintaining an inclusive and psychologically safe culture, where you are encouraged and empowered to take responsibility while leading both yourself and others. We combine this with a substantial focus on continuously staying relevant and being a meaningful social community to our people. We are a people’s business, and therefore we strongly believe that this is an essential prerequisite for making an impact that truly matters – for ourselves and for our clients**.**

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for you, who are passionate about consulting and the CFO-area and who are willing to go the extra mile to deliver sustainable impact that truly matters to our clients. You show an eagerness to make a difference for both clients and colleagues and you are able to see the opportunities and potential in all types of assignments. As our business can be highly changeable, it is important that you are curious by nature, and that you face challenges with an open-minded and solution-oriented approach.

In addition to this, you:

• Have completed a master’s degree within the fields of finance, economics, business, accounting, social sciences, IT, or similar areas in the summer of 2027 or before

• Have achieved academic results from your bachelor’s and master’s degree that you are proud of

• Demonstrate a flair for both oral and written communication and are fluent in English

• Have a legal working permit in Denmark

Although relevant job experience might be an advantage, this is not a requirement.

Want to know more?

Click the "I'm interested"-button above and upload your CV and grade transcripts from your bachelor’s and master’s degree if you are interested and ready to join our team**. Instead of an application letter, we would like you to answer the questions you will be presented with on the next pages** (please only consider the required (*) fields). As we process applications and arrange interviews on an ongoing basis, we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Application deadline: Hiring on an ongoing basis.

Please do not hesitate to contact Giulio Marano (gimarano@deloitte.dk / +45 30 93 64 11) or Maria Banke (mbanke@deloitte.dk / +45 20 97 64 15) if you have any questions about the position.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: Senior Associate, Global Clinical Drug Supply Execution
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

Genmab is searching for an energized Senior Associate to be part of Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery team in Copenhagen within commute distance from our office locations to work according to your hybrid work arrangement.

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. During inspections, you will participate in back-office activities and help ensure timely retrieval and follow-up of requested information.

The role also offers opportunities to develop beyond inspection readiness. Working closely with Clinical Supply Managers in the Portfolio & Project Delivery team and colleagues across the department, you will support selected operational tasks and initiatives while gaining broader exposure to clinical trial management. Through collaboration with Clinical Trial Operations and CROs, and hands-on involvement in clinical supply activities, you will further develop your GCP and clinical supply knowledge.

The position is based in Copenhagen.

**Responsibilities

**

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support activities related to day-to-day trial management, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Support distribution and logistics, including tasks related to shipment documentation, in alignment with the Drug Supply Managers.

• Build knowledge of especially GCP but also GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery function

• Participate in maintenance and continuous improvement of procedures, tools and ways of working supporting inspection readiness and clinical supply activities.

• Responsible for being compliant with Genmab´s quality system.

**Requirements

**

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GCP and GMP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GCP/GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functional with internal and external stakeholders.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

**The Team

**You will be part of a highly competent team focused on end-to-end trial management including planning and maintenance of supplies for clinical trials, working closely with cross-functional stakeholders in both CMC and Clinical Trial Operations.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department. We foster a supportive, international, and fast-paced work environment centered on collaboration, excellence, and a can-do attitude to achieve results.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).
